title: 5 Signs You Need Sleeping Gummies for Better Sleep
htmlContent:
Sleep deprivation afflicts millions worldwide. According to conservative estimates, 10% of the global adult population suffers from insomnia, with another 20% experiencing insomnia symptoms occasionally. The actual picture might be way grimmer if you consider that insomnia is but one of numerous sleep disorders. Others include sleep apnea, REM behavior disorder, and restless leg syndrome. Sleep disorders can stem from different causes. The symptoms may also be varied depending on the condition’s underlying cause, trigger factors, and extent of progression. Sleeping gummies gained significant attention for their remarkable ability to boost sleep quality. These products are preferable to conventional sleep pills due to their lower propensity for adverse effects. This post highlights the five tell-tale signs that it’s time to invest in sleeping gummies.

What Are Sleeping Gummies?

Sleeping gummies, as the name implies, are chews widely touted as sleep aids. They typically contain melatonin supplements. Melatonin is a natural hormone secreted by the brain's pineal glands, which regulates our circadian rhythms. However, the ability to produce melatonin naturally varies by age and overall health. Several findings suggest that older and the chronically ill secrete less melatonin than younger and healthier folk. Interestingly, the efficiency of melatonin secretion may vary even among the healthy population. That explains the growing interest in melatonin-containing supplements like sleeping gummies. Besides melatonin, sleeping gummies may be fortified with renowned sleep-aiding compounds like L-theanine and cannabidiol (CBD). L-theanine is a naturally occurring hormone that’s also available in supplements, while CBD is a cannabis-derived compound that constitutes the plant’s 100+ phytocannabinoids. Photo Credit: Pixabay.com

  1. Longer Sleep Latency

  Sleep latency refers to the average time it takes to drift from complete wakefulness to sleep after turning off the lights. It’s also known simply as sleep onset time. Most healthy people have a sleep onset time between 10 and 20 minutes. While a shorter sleep latency is desirable, taking much longer to fall asleep can impact your sleep routine and overall health. Note that multiple factors may prolong your sleep onset time. For instance, underlying anxiety disorders or certain drugs can trigger nervousness at bedtime, making it harder to drift off to sleep. Similarly, consumable products like coffee can increase sleep latency by stimulating mental alertness. It’s important to rule out these factors before taking sleep-aiding gummies. If the problem persists beyond several weeks despite taking sleeping gummies regularly, that’s your cue to seek professional medical advice.

  1. Frequent Sleep Disruptions

  Taking longer to fall asleep is difficult enough for insomniacs. But the real challenge is the inability to sleep for longer hour blocks. According to experts, normal adults require 7 – 9 hours of sleep every night (or every 24 hours, depending on your daily schedules). Healthy children and infants can sleep up to 16 hours a day. Falling short of the recommended daily sleep duration may trigger a wide spectrum of health issues, including insomnia and anxiety disorders. Fortunately, you can administer sleeping gummies to treat certain medical causes of sleep disruptions. For instance, gummies formulated with cannabidiol may alleviate post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms, including flashbacks and nightmares. Non-medical causes, such as frequent urination and environmental factors, can be addressed through appropriate lifestyle adjustments. Note that sleeping way longer than recommended can be equally harmful to your health. Like sleep deprivation, oversleeping has been linked to daytime grogginess and drowsiness.

  1. Drowsiness

  We’ve just hinted at drowsiness as a potential consequence of sleep deprivation. Drowsiness is often described as ‘prolonged feelings of unexplained fatigue.’ However, “unexplained” is a misnomer, as the condition is typically due to sleeplessness. Drowsiness can cause a need for daytime naps. In fact, most people will inadvertently fall asleep at inappropriate times and places. But even after napping, the lethargic feelings may persist. Fatigue symptoms typically manifest in the eyes and legs, although the entire body may be affected. Feelings of drowsiness may further cause mental fogginess. This refers to an inability to think clearly or make rational decisions. Additional mental symptoms include irritability, nervousness, and forgetfulness. While the majority of drowsiness cases are linked to sleep deprivation, the condition may also result from unrelated factors like substance abuse, caffeine withdrawal, and medication side effects. Identifying the underlying cause is important before administering sleeping gummies. Photo Credit: Pixabay.com

  1. Diminished Attention Span

  Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is probably the first thing that comes to mind when discussing impaired mental concentration. However, reduced attention span may also spring from sleep-related causes like insomnia. Studies have established a direct correlation between sleep deprivation and impaired attention span. In fact, inadequate sleep can impair most other cognitive functions, including learning and memory consolidation. People with diminished attention span may struggle to focus on simple tasks even when not necessarily distracted. This could affect daytime productivity, resulting in poor workplace or school performance. If you’re a stay-at-home parent, reduced mental concentration can present challenges in completing your daily house chores. Now, it’s normal to lose your focus while distracted or multi-tasking. Emotional factors, such as receiving shocking news, may also throw you off balance. But if you constantly struggle to stay on task without reasonable distractions, it’s best to incorporate sleeping gummies into your wellness routine. Sleeping gummies will reinvigorate your mind by helping you repay the sleep debt causing impaired attention span.

  1. Depression

  This is perhaps the most worrisome of all the reasons to take sleeping gummies. Depression doesn’t occur overnight. It’s usually a result of untreated medical conditions, including insomnia. According to research, chronic insomnia may lead to depression and other psychological disorders. That’s due to its effects on the brain’s normal functioning. Additional findings suggest that insomniacs are over ten times more likely to develop depression, with up to 75% of depression cases directly attributable to sleeplessness. First, prolonged sleeplessness ramps up the secretion of the stress hormone cortisol. Untreated stress can develop into an anxiety disorder, which eventually degenerates into clinical depression. Loss of interest in pleasurable activities, seclusion, and foul moods are all depressive symptoms to watch out for. Consuming sleeping gummies might help manage the condition before it escalates to life-threatening signs, such as suicidal tendencies. Besides boosting sleep quality, most sleeping gummies contain “feel-good” neurotransmitters that can reverse depression by diminishing cortisol production. Photo Credit: Pixabay.com

The Bottom Line

The ability of sleeping gummies to boost sleep quality is well-documented. However, the safety of these supplements depends on their chief active ingredients. For the best outcome, insist on gummies formulated with sleep-aiding compounds like melatonin and cannabidiol. Remember to also administer the products following the recommendations of a licensed medical practitioner.
